title: Warehouse Safety Monitoring
summary: Use existing or added CCTV to spot forklift and pedestrian near-misses, missing PPE, blocked fire exits and people in restricted zones, with alerts to supervisors and evidence for safety reviews.

seo.title: AI Warehouse Safety Monitoring with CCTV | VipraTech
seo.description: Computer vision on warehouse CCTV that flags forklift near-misses, missing PPE, blocked exits and restricted-zone entry, with supervisor alerts.

problem.intro: Warehouses mix forklifts, reach trucks, pallet jacks and people in tight aisles and busy docks, often with contract labour across shifts. Safety teams rely on walk-rounds and reported incidents, so near-misses that nobody reports stay invisible until someone is hurt.

pain_points.title: Near-misses go unreported
pain_points.detail: Forklift and pedestrian close calls are rarely reported, so the same dangerous spots stay unaddressed.

pain_points.title: PPE use varies by shift
pain_points.detail: Safety shoes, high-visibility vests and helmets are worn during audits and dropped on night shifts and during peak loading.

pain_points.title: Blocked exits and aisles
pain_points.detail: Pallets left in fire exits, marked walkways or in front of fire equipment are found only during periodic inspections.

pain_points.title: Dock and vehicle risks
pain_points.detail: People standing behind reversing trucks or near open dock edges are a known risk that supervisors cannot watch continuously.

solution.overview: We build safety analytics on your CCTV, adding cameras only where coverage is missing. Models run on an edge server at the site and detect forklifts, people and PPE, with zones drawn for walkways, docks, racking aisles and fire exits. The system raises alerts for near-misses between vehicles and pedestrians, missing PPE in mandatory zones, entry into restricted areas and obstructed exits. Alerts reach supervisors on a dashboard or WhatsApp with a short clip. A weekly report shows hotspots by zone and shift, so the EHS team can fix layouts and training rather than chase individuals.
capabilities: Detects forklift and pedestrian proximity and near-miss events in aisles and docks
Checks for safety shoes, high-visibility vests and helmets in mandatory zones
Flags blocked fire exits, walkways and fire equipment
Detects entry into restricted zones such as racking under maintenance or dock edges
Sends alerts with short clips to supervisors on a dashboard or WhatsApp
Produces hotspot reports by zone, shift and event type

workflow.title: Map zones and rules
workflow.detail: With the EHS team we draw zones on each camera view and agree the rules and alert recipients for each.

workflow.title: Process video on site
workflow.detail: Camera streams are processed on a site server, so video does not need to leave the premises.

workflow.title: Detect events
workflow.detail: Models detect near-misses, PPE gaps, restricted-zone entry and obstructions.

workflow.title: Filter and alert
workflow.detail: Events above the confidence threshold go to the supervisor with a clip; the rest are logged for weekly review.

workflow.title: Supervisor action
workflow.detail: The supervisor confirms or dismisses the alert and records the action taken.

workflow.title: Review hotspots
workflow.detail: Weekly reports show patterns by zone and shift for the EHS team and site leadership.

inputs: CCTV streams from aisles, docks and exits
Site layout with zones and PPE rules
outputs: Log of confirmed and dismissed events
Hotspot reports by zone, shift and event type
Evidence for safety reviews and toolbox talks
human_in_the_loop: Supervisors confirm or dismiss every alert and record the action taken. The EHS team decides corrective actions from the hotspot reports, and the system is not used for automated disciplinary action.
integrations: Existing CCTV and NVR (RTSP or ONVIF)
WhatsApp Business API or SMS gateway
WMS for shift and zone context
Access control system for restricted areas
guardrails: Video processed on site, with only short clips of confirmed events stored
Face blurring in reports where identification is not needed
Clear signage and worker notice about camera analytics
Alert thresholds tuned with supervisors to avoid alert fatigue
Clip access restricted by role and logged
compliance_notes: Supports employer safety duties under India's Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code 2020 and your site safety management system.
Workers are data principals under the DPDP Act 2023, so purpose, notice, retention and access are defined before go-live.

pilot.scope: One warehouse, focused on a few high-risk areas such as the inbound dock and a busy forklift aisle, using existing cameras where possible.
deliverables: Zone and rule configuration for the pilot areas
Pilot report on alert quality and hotspots

what_we_measure.how: Alerts that supervisors confirm as genuine events, out of all alerts raised.
Events found in sampled footage reviews compared with alerts raised.
Time from alert to confirmation and action in the event log.
Corrective actions recorded by EHS against reported hotspots.

faqs.q: Can we use our existing CCTV cameras?
faqs.a: Usually for aisles and exits, if resolution and angle are adequate. Docks and blind spots sometimes need extra cameras, which the coverage assessment identifies.

faqs.q: Will workers be identified and penalised?
faqs.a: The system is designed to find unsafe conditions and patterns, not to discipline individuals. Faces can be blurred in reports, and how alerts are used is your policy decision, which we recommend sharing with workers.
No. Processing runs on an edge server at the site. Only short clips of confirmed events and summary reports are stored, with retention you define.

faqs.q: How do you avoid too many false alerts?
faqs.a: Zones and thresholds are tuned with supervisors during the pilot, and low-confidence detections go to a weekly review log instead of real-time alerts. Alert precision is measured and reported.
